title: American Yellowwood: Ancient American Yellowwoods You Can Visit
meta_description: One of the rarest native trees of eastern North America. Bartram's Garden has a yellowwood over 200 years old that lightning struck in 2010.
intro: American yellowwood grows wild only on a scatter of hillsides in Kentucky, Tennessee and the western Carolinas, and it is named for the bright yellow heartwood once boiled down for dye. The oldest of ours is at Bartram's Garden in Philadelphia, over 200 years old, hollow and held together with wire. In June 2010 a storm struck it, WHYY reported that it tore off six limbs and left one, and the garden now describes it as recovering and still blooming. Ottawa has one in Major's Hill Park, well over a thousand kilometres north of the species' range. In Tilburg, a yellowwood of about 70 years stands in the collection around the old municipal nursery, where evening students once learned tree names along a path they called the sweat lane.
